title: Config file to run & debug Serge from VS-Code
body: Fixes #1858 We are able to debug: - client package - jest Working on how to debug cross packages like from clients -> components...

comments_data.body: @philb89 - could you give me some instructions on how to use this please?

> @philb89 - could you give me some instructions on how to use this please?

Hi @IanMayo, it's pretty simple to use, so here is the steps:
Debug in Client package:
![Screen Shot 2023-03-26 at 9 56 58 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26705621/227752813-2b9efa44-8b11-46ef-aef3-037baa4bdf56.png)
- Click Run and Debug section (1) -> click on green button (2) to start debug mode
- Run `yarn develop` from terminal
![Screen Shot 2023-03-26 at 9 54 47 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26705621/227752863-63d1f856-465a-464b-8006-fe26f2607a0f.png)
- Add breakpoint in the vscode and tadaa !!!

Debug unit tests with Jest is more simple, you will see 2 sections:
- Jest All: run all Jest tests with debug mode
- Jest Current File: run the active jest with debug mode
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26705621/227753915-8e73ce8c-6f37-4bf9-8843-9a2397f1af63.png)
This is brilliant @lebaphi - I wish we had this years ago :-)

issues.title: Config file to run & debug Serge from VS-Code
issues.body:
I've just read an article that demonstrates how to debug a node-js app from within VS-Code:
https://dev.to/profydev/how-to-debug-react-apps-with-vs-code-boost-your-debugging-productivity-1k05

I've run debuggers for other languages (Java esp), and enjoyed viewing variables and setting breakpoints.

Hmm, but the article seems to expect a monolith repo - with all code in one folder - but we have a monorepo, with multiple packages.

Could you experiment and see if its possible to produce a `launch.json` file that works for all of our packages?

If we can't do it for all of our packages, then just for `components` would be good.

[Here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/56260686/debugging-a-lerna-typescript-project-in-vscode) is an article that may be related.

Aah, it would also be good to configure VS-code to let us debug `Jest` unit tests,  too: https://www.basefactor.com/using-visual-studio-code-to-debug-jest-based-unit-tests
